title: Restore Supabase migration-history correspondence via non-executable historical receipts

sha_binding.verified_source_note: The merge commit that synced this branch to main after its blocking lane UTV2-1783 merged, and the last non-proof commit on this branch. Every CI receipt in this bundle was re-captured at this exact head; the previous anchor 63478030 is superseded because the sync introduced non-proof files after it, which proof-binding-validator correctly rejected. Only proof-path commits follow this anchor. merge_sha stays null pre-merge per the schema-v2 evidence contract (CEP-E7); post-merge-lane-close.yml binds it to the real merge commit.

verdict.statement: supabase db push refused to run against production at all, because 127 remote migration-ledger versions had no local counterpart. Each now has a non-executable receipt that binds the exact SQL that executed and asserts baseline subsumption. Correspondence is restored against live production (remote_only=0) and the sanctioned dry-run proposes exactly one migration.

receipt_replay_drill.workflow: migration-reversibility-gate / Schema round-trip drill (scratch Postgres — all new migrations)
receipt_replay_drill.detail: Behaviour-level, not file inspection. Baseline applied to a clean database in its own scratch DB; all 127 receipts replayed under ON_ERROR_STOP=1; catalog fingerprint over relations, columns, constraints and function identities identical before and after; the six active forward migrations then replayed on top.
receipt_replay_drill.non_vacuity_control: Phase 1 refuses below a floor of 200 catalog entries. Without it, a baseline that silently failed to apply would leave both fingerprints empty and identical and the drill would report PASS having proven nothing. The first CI execution reported '1 catalog entries' — a line-counting artefact of COPY ... TO STDOUT escaping newlines — which is why the floor and per-row output were added rather than the number being explained away.

precondition_drill.detail: All 127 receipts returned a named pass: a receipt executes no statement, so it has no fail-closed precondition to drill. Reported as a result rather than skipped, so the job's own 'a run that drilled nothing is not a pass' backstop still sees one result per counted file.
cases: all 127 new migrations are verified non-executable historical version receipts — each returned a named pass rather than being skipped, so the job's 'a run that drilled nothing is not a pass' backstop saw one result per counted file (drilled 127)

applies on an empty scratch database — in job 100073671950 of the same run, a freshly created scratch database took the baseline plus all 127 receipts under ON_ERROR_STOP=1, reaching 1396 catalog entries; this lane adds no object-creating migration, so successful application on an empty target is demonstrated by that replay rather than by a refusal-drill apply case
a receipt that gains an executable statement loses the exemption and is required to declare a fail-closed precondition — proven by mutation, not by inspection

reversibility_gate.detail: migration-reversibility-gate.ts exempts verified non-executable receipts from the down-script requirement. The gate's own 7 adversarial tests still pass.

production_correspondence.capture_method: CAPTURE METHOD — run by the orchestrator from the lane worktree against the linked production project. Read-only `supabase migration list --linked` and `supabase db push --linked --dry-run`. No CI job in this repo can produce this: no workflow holds a production database credential. Carries no run or job id and is weaker than the four receipted drill fields. Re-derivable by re-running the same two commands.

ledger_extraction.method: Supabase Management API query endpoint (POST /v1/projects/{ref}/database/query), authenticated with the CLI access token, read straight to disk.
ledger_extraction.why: The alternative was passing ~76KB of historical SQL through a model context and retyping it, where one altered byte would silently corrupt preserved history. Every artifact is a direct copy of what the ledger returned.

schema_roundtrip_drill.workflow: migration-reversibility-gate / Schema round-trip drill (scratch Postgres — all new migrations)
schema_roundtrip_drill.detail: Job passed. Stated precisely so it is not over-read: all 127 new migrations are non-executable receipts and were exempted from the apply/rollback/reapply cycle, because a receipt executes nothing and its only possible down script is a no-op the reversibility gate itself rejects as comment-only. No convergence cycle was therefore exercised by this lane's files. The substantive behavioural evidence in this same job is runtime_proof.receipt_replay_drill, which applies the baseline and all 127 receipts to a clean database and compares catalog fingerprints.

live_schema_parity.workflow: Live Schema Parity / Live Schema Parity
live_schema_parity.detail: Repo migration set diffed against the live production database: no unauthorized findings. Expected — this lane adds no schema object. Every receipt is comments-only, so the expected schema is unchanged from main, which is itself corroboration that the 127 receipts introduce no DDL.

writable_db_proof_staging.detail: Run-scoped staging receipt produced in the staging-ci environment against xskgrzbteyqdufktjrjx, inside the REQUIRED verify workflow run at this exact head, so the receipt and the required check are the same run and cannot drift apart. No production credential is reachable from this job.

divergences.policy: The ledger payload is executed-history truth and is what source_sha256 binds. The archive file is retained unchanged as later-edited intent at archive_intent_path. The two are deliberately not reconciled.
divergences.correction_note: An earlier audit reported 3. Re-measured with a normaliser that strips SQL comments, 202604300003 differs from its archive only by a UTV2-868 recovery comment. A comment cannot have executed, so it is not an executed-SQL divergence. Stated explicitly rather than quietly adjusted.

double_applied_versions.detail: Same logical migration applied twice under two different version strings. Two are proven by the later row's name embedding its partner's version (20260427045252, 20260509160906); four share a UTV2 slug. All six pairs have different source hashes — the second application executed different SQL, not a replay of the first.

alias_versions.detail: Remote rows whose name references a migration still present in the active replay path. Re-executing them would duplicate objects the baseline already creates.

scope.authorization: PM-approved scope expansion recorded in Linear; bounded to two hunks (+29/-0).
scope.mechanical_note: file_scope_lock widening is inert from the head side by design (scripts/ci/file-scope-guard.ts resolves the lock from the first commit that added the manifest). This PR therefore requires an externally-authored scope-override/v1 comment from a CODEOWNERS reviewer against the final head. Not self-issued.
